elements with id attributes, but the acceptance tests expect the enterprise tier to be rendered as an
(which aligns) while other tiers are also expected to be
. However, the task specification states that tier cards should be

elements. In the current code, the renderTier function uses
for all tiers, so that matches; however, the test 'Enterprise card is premium with the atrium photo' checks for an and expects a 'Premium' label and an img with src containing 'enterprise-atrium', which is satisfied. The problem lies elsewhere. The Layout of the EngagementsPage includes a
after the tier cards, but the acceptance test expects the Not sure line to be below the tiers and not inside any article, which matches the code. The issue is that the EngagementsPage does not include a
with class name "engagements-section" or any explicit container class that the tests might use to locate the Not sure line. The test uses `deepest(main, 'Not sure which fits?')` and then checks that the element is after the last tier card (). This should pass. However, the test also expects that the enterprise tier be rendered as an
element with id="enterprise" and includes a Premium label. The code adds class "premium" but does not add explicit text "Premium" in a visible element; it adds a Premium which should be found. That seems correct. The probably failing test is the `home content additions` test for the audience panels: it expects `PANELS[0].text` to be a string with two sentences, but the content defines the field `text` (not `text` in the test but they refer to `p.text`). In the test code, they access `PANELS[0].text` but the content defines property name `text`. This matches. The test also checks that the panel has a link 'Enterprise engagements' for the second panel, but the enterprise panel's link label is 'Enterprise engagements', which matches. However, they also check that the 'Small and medium-sized businesses' panel does not contain a link to '/engagements#enterprise', which is true. The test expects the image src to contain 'smb-owner' and 'enterprise-atrium' which match. The home page rendering tests check for the presence of the systems band and capabilities. The Systems band heading is 'Systems built to be observed and sustained', which matches. However, they also check that the capabilities have exactly 4 items and each title matches CAPABILITIES titles. In content, CAPABILITIES includes titles matching. The description for each capability must be a single sentence; they check `sentenceCount(c.description) === 1`. Each description in CAPABILITIES ends with a period and has no additional sentence, matching. So far no obvious mismatch. But the acceptance test `home page redesign rendering` checks the order of sections at the end (h1, credibility strip, audience panel, systems band, pillar card, how we work, example engagements, testimonial, why, CTA). It expects that after the credibility strip (checked via points), the next element is the SMB panel, identified by the text 'Small and medium-sized businesses'. In the code, after the hero, the HomePage component likely renders the credibility strip followed by the audience panels. The implementation details (not shown) may have the panels in a different order or container, causing order test failure. Also there is a missing import/export of the EXAMPLES_SECTION variable (used only in content but not referenced in any page). The HomePage likely does not render the examples section or examples. The tests for examples check that each example section renders with proper tags, but if HomePage does not include those sections, the test would fail. Indeed, the test 'example engagements section' searches for a heading 'The kinds of systems we build' and expects each example to be present. If HomePage does not render EXAMPLES_SECTION or EXAMPLES, that test fails. So the code likely is missing rendering for these new sections (audience panels, systems band, capability cards, operate step, examples, testimonial). Therefore the implementation does not fully satisfy the redesign requirements and is missing required content rendering, causing test failures. The solution must add the missing sections and ensure the order and content match the tests.

Missing required implementations: The new content fields defined in src/content/home.ts (CREDIBILITY_POINTS, AUDIENCE_PANELS, SYSTEMS_BAND, CAPABILITIES, OPERATE_STEP, EXAMPLES_SECTION, EXAMPLES, TESTIMONIAL) are not rendered in HomePage, causing tests for credibility strip, audience panels, systems band, capabilities, operate step, examples, and testimonial to fail.

Missing required implementations: The new sections for SystemsPage (system sections, deliverables, CTA band) are not fully rendered as per the tests (e.g., the system sections need specific class names, eyebrow order, and proper ids). Ensure the System sections have the correct structure and class names expected by tests.

Missing required implementations: The EngagementsPage does not render a section with class "not-sure" containing the "Not sure which fits?" line as a separate block below the tier cards (tests check for its position). Ensure the Not sure line is rendered correctly and not inside a card.

Missing required implementations: The ArchitectureDiagram component must be used on both the Systems page and the Home page systems band. Ensure the component is imported and rendered correctly in HomePage (currently missing) and that it complies with accessibility tests (title, desc, labels, monospace).
open_notes: Missing updated design tokens: src/styles/theme.css does not define the required new CSS custom properties (--color-navy-deep #071528, --color-surface-teal #F2F7F7, --color-hairline #E3E8EF, --font-mono). Without these, requirements R14, R15, R16, R17, R18, R20, R28, R30, R31, R32, R33, R34, R36, R37, R38, R40, R41, R44‑R51, R53‑R58, R59‑R61, R70‑R71, R72‑R76, and many other UI and logic requirements referencing these tokens cannot be satisfied.
The theme token file src/theme/tokens.ts likely does not mirror the new tokens either (not inspected but likely missing), causing mismatch with the token mirroring requirement.

Missing or incomplete implementation of the hero overlay gradient and bell‑curve motif on the home hero: the new design calls for a navy gradient overlay and a BellCurveMotif behind the hero, but the code does not show these elements being rendered.

Missing implementation of the ArchitectureDiagram component variant handling: the component currently renders both wide and stacked SVGs always, but the spec requires the stacked variant to be hidden (display:none) on desktop and visible on phones, with proper CSS. No CSS appears to hide one of the diagrams.

Missing implementation of the new pages (/systems, /engagements) meta tags and Open Graph properties: while the SEO data includes titles and descriptions, the og:type and og:url tags are not properly set for these pages (they default to generic values). The spec requires explicit og:url matching the site URL plus path and og:type "website".
The contact form does not include the optional "Company size" select field: src/lib/contactForm.ts defines COMPANY_SIZE_OPTIONS, but src/pages/ContactPage.tsx does not render a <select> for it.

The navigation header and footer link sets do not match the required order: tests expect the header nav to include Services, Systems, Training, Engagements, About, Contact plus a CTA. The current site content may still have the old order or missing Links.

The ArchitectureDiagram component adds two SVGs (wide and stacked) always, causing duplicate diagram content and violating the requirement that on phones a second stacked variant should be hidden via CSS without duplication for screen readers. The current implementation renders both SVGs with class "arch-stacked" always, not conditionally hidden, and both have accessible <title> and <desc> (mounted true after hydration) potentially causing duplicate content for screen readers. The task requires the stacked variant to be hidden via CSS (display:none) and not be aria-hidden, and only one set of <title>/<desc> needed. Adjust ArchitectureDiagram to render a single SVG for desktop and conditionally hide the stacked one with CSS (e.g., using media queries and `aria-hidden` appropriately).

EngagementsPage renders Enterprise tier card as <article id="enterprise">, but the test expects a generic element with id "enterprise" (not necessarily article) and specifically checks that the enterprise card is wrapped in <article>. However the test suite's weak_tests indicate that this expectation is questionable. The test currently fails because it expects the enterprise card to be an <article> element, but the task only requires an element with id "enterprise" (any tag). The implementation uses <article>, which may cause failure in tests expecting a different element type. Align the markup to the test expectation by using a generic <section> or <div> with id "enterprise" instead of <article>.

EngagementsPage includes a "Not sure which fits?" line inside a <section class="not-sure"> but the test expects it to be placed below the tiers and not inside an article element. The current structure may not match test ordering expectations; adjust the placement to ensure the line appears after the tier cards and before any other container, and ensure it doesn't contain an article tag.
